evidence.text: The entry describes 你 as a pronoun for singular second person, absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and Shuowen. It cites 集韻·止韻, “你，汝也,” and 隋書·李密傳 as examples, then separately notes later and modern use. These citations establish the dictionary’s reported evidence, but do not independently date the wording of the 隋書 passage to the narrated events.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 你

evidence.field: 說文釋形、字樣說明、釋義、形體資料表
evidence.text: The entry says 你 is not in Shuowen and describes its right-hand shape as 尔. It records the 集韻 gloss “你，乃里切。汝也” and a second-person use from 周書, and gives examples of plural, possessive, and generic uses from later works. It also indexes 集韻 pages 311 and 325. The list of senses is not, by itself, a dated semantic chronology.
evidence.title: Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》: 你

evidence.field: 尔 entry; 形義通解; 字形資料
evidence.text: The entry says the bronze form of 尔/尒 is made by taking the upper part of 爾, and calls it a shortened form of 爾. It reports 尔/爾 uses for ‘you/your’, including bronze and Warring States manuscript examples, and says 尔 later developed into modern 你. This supports the reported historical relationship and word use of 尔, but does not independently establish a phonetic role for 尔 in 你.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 尔

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart
evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction table, 尔 row
evidence.text: The 2014 Baxter–Sagart reconstruction table gives 尔 (Mandarin ěr) Middle Chinese nyeX and Old Chinese *n[ə][r]ʔ, glossed ‘you(r)’. It provides a reconstruction for 尔, but this inspected table did not supply a 你 row, so a within-system comparison for the proposed 你–尔 sound relationship cannot be made from it here. Preserve this source’s notation; it is not the same reconstruction system as Zhengzhang.

gaps: No inspected primary paleographic source directly analyzes 你 as phono-semantic or ideographic. The dossier’s competing formation accounts therefore remain unresolved; 亻 as semantic and 尔 as phonetic is plausible in secondary accounts but not established by the inspected primary-style entries.

CUHK reports no 你 in oracle-bone or bronze inscriptions and no entry in Shuowen. Earliest attested written form was not established beyond the cited 集韻 entry and quoted historical texts; their textual witnesses and the dating of the quoted wording need specialist verification.

The sound role of 尔 in the proposed 你 compound is not directly documented by the opened graph-history entries. Baxter–Sagart supplies a reading for 尔 but no matched 你 row was inspected. Local Baxter–Sagart data supplied in the input contains an 尔 row only, so it cannot establish the pair’s comparison.

Current readings from local Unihan rows are metadata only. Official per-character Unicode records for U+4F60 and U+5C14 could not be accessed. No independently verified current reading for 尔 is therefore claimed beyond the supplied local row and dictionary material.

The reviewed sources report later plural, possessive, and generic uses but do not establish a dated sequence or the semantic links among them. No external evidence here establishes graphic corruption in the history of 你.

No suitable historical glyph image with verified identity and reuse rights was established. The Commons small-seal image is explicitly a modern font-based redraw and is not an ancient form; CUHK glyphs were not confirmed reusable, and Xiaoxuetang record pages could not be accessed. No image candidate is proposed. No bulk extract is recommended.

limitations.text: Inspected the Commons file page for a small-seal-style 你 glyph; it explicitly identifies the image as a computer-font construction and says 你 did not exist in seal script. It is therefore excluded as historical evidence. CUHK displays 尔 bronze and small-seal examples, but the page’s reuse terms for those specific glyph images were not verified. Xiaoxuetang direct record pages were inaccessible, so no licensed historical image could be selected.
